title: SDK Developer Surface Stability and Adaptive Retry Guidelines (Python/TS/Go)
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Purpose: Produce a concise, cross-language developer-facing requirements doc that defines expected semantics for pagination cursors, streaming chunk boundaries, client-side idempotency keys, and an adaptive retry/backoff policy. This PRD consolidates prior scattered notes, resolves ambiguous behaviors flagged in SDK reviews, and defines an explicit compatibility/deprecation window to give engineering teams clear upgrade paths.

Scope: Python/TypeScript/Go SDKs only; surface-level behavioral contracts (not low-level transport). Covers: page-oriented pagination (cursor tokens and offsets), resumable streaming (chunk framing and finalization), retry categories (idempotent vs non-idempotent paths), adaptive backoff defaults, and graceful degradation rules for mixed-version clients and servers.

Out of scope: language-specific syntactic sugar beyond the client surface, sampling/temperature semantics, server implementation details beyond observable contract, and Dedicated/private deployment infra changes not affecting the API contract.
acceptance_criteria: Published SDK requirements doc approved by SDK working group (PM, 2x SDK leads, 1x runtime engineer, 1x QA)
Reference test suite with 50+ deterministic cases (pagination/resume/retry) that passes on all three language SDKs in CI
Default retry/backoff policy implemented in Python/TS/Go SDKs and exercised in integration smoke tests (latency and error budget preserved)
Streaming contract documented with examples: chunk boundaries, finalization event, resume semantics for partial chunks
Compatibility matrix and deprecation schedule published (minimum 6 months notice for breaking changes)
decision_log: 2026-03-03: Agreed to use opaque cursor tokens for page state; cursor lifetime is server-defined. Clients should treat cursors as opaque and never derive semantics from their structure. (Decision by PM, SDK leads)

2026-03-05: Retry taxonomy accepted: classify errors into transient (retryable), throttling (retry with quota-aware backoff), and permanent (no retry). Default attempts: 3 for transient, 5 for throttling with exponential jitter. (Decision by runtime/infra)

2026-03-07: Streaming framing: use application-level chunk delimiters (JSON-lines for text streams, length-prefixed for binary). Streams must emit a finalization marker event ("stream_end") to indicate completion. Client resume allowed only at chunk boundaries. (Decision by SDK and protocol teams)

2026-03-10: Idempotency keys: Clients should expose an optional idempotencyKey param for mutation-like endpoints; SDK will auto-generate v4 UUIDs when not provided and surface policy in docs. Server will de-duplicate at least 60 seconds; server-side window documented in compatibility table. (Decision by PM + Security)

2026-03-12: Backwards compatibility window: guarantee non-breaking behavior for 12 months. Breaking changes allowed only with a deprecation notice and migration guide published at least 6 months prior. (Decision by leadership)

2026-03-13: Opt-in adaptive retry: SDKs will expose an opt-in adaptive mode that reduces retries under client-detected high error rates to protect latency SLOs. Default remains conservative retry policy. (Decision during engineering review)
comments: 2026-03-02 - Aisha Patel: Initial draft posted. Key ask: unambiguously define the behavior clients should expect when resuming paginated reads and streaming interruptions. Need buy-in on cursor semantics.

2026-03-04 - Marcus Chen: Engineering requests that the retry policy include a maximum total retry time window to avoid unbounded client hang (proposal: 30s default, configurable). Added to decision queue.

2026-03-06 - Lina Morales (SDK Lead, TS): Reviewed streaming framing -- prefer length-prefixed binary for WebSocket/HTTP2 binary streams; JSON-lines for text. Will prototype both in the SDKs. Action: prototype small shim by 2026-03-11.

2026-03-08 - Tomas Becker (Runtime): Noted that server-side cursor invalidation can occur on model-rollout; suggested adding a migration example in docs and tests to cover invalidated cursor behavior.
2026-03-11 - QA (Neha Singh): Proposed 12 negative tests for mid-stream cancellation and resume; moving to the acceptance test CSV. Will run in canary CI.

2026-03-13 - Marcus Chen: Implemented reference adaptive-backoff algorithm in test harness (exponential with full jitter + circuit-breaker after 10 failures). PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-proposals/pull/142
